verifier_notes.method: Independent re-check in the Higgsfield sandbox: Commons API (wikitext, rendered licence box via action=parse, extmetadata, structured data via wbgetentities, revision histories, logevents), curl -sIL and full download of every media_url with ffprobe and sha1, Wayback CDX/id_ fetches, developer primary sources (MiniMax, THUDM GitHub + Hugging Face Space source at the December-2024 revision, Lightricks GitHub + licences, ByteDance Seed, xAI news/ToS via Wayback), and pixel statistics (temporal variance, min-projection, template matching, image registration). No frame was ever viewed by a human or described by a vision tool; the six Higgsfield video analyses queued by H3 were still 'queued' when polled, so nothing below is a visual description.
verifier_notes.global_caveat: Every candidate except the Grok clip and the Cybertruck clip rests wholly or partly on the Commons {{PD-algorithm}} community tag (US-law basis: no human authorship). The rendered tag itself warns: 'there is a risk that AI-generated media uploaded on Commons may violate the rights of the authors of the original works' and that the UK and Hong Kong give computer-generated works 50 years of protection. Platform terms are a residual risk for the Hailuo, Grok and CogVideoX-Space clips (see per-clip conditions).

issues_found: Licence cannot be established: the only licence text is {{PD-algorithm}} applied by a third-party uploader (5lensiu, 10 edits, UploadWizard 'PD-algorithm upload' on 2026-02-14). The uploader did not generate the clip, gives no dedication, and the Author field 'Seedance 2.0/Bytedance' is only a claimed attribution.

Source is not ByteDance: seedance2.ai is an independent commercial generator site. Wayback shows it live from 2025-11-27 (about 11 weeks before the official 2026-02-12 Seedance 2.0 launch) under the 'Seedance 2' brand, with fabricated-looking testimonials, its own Terms of Service/Privacy/Refund pages and the footer 'Copyright (c) 2026 Seedance2.ai All rights reserved.' No ByteDance affiliation is stated. The official product page is seed.bytedance.com/en/seedance2_0.

Model claim unverifiable: the site's older gallery folder (cdn.seedance2.ai/examples/seedance/, captured 2025-11-27) shows it displayed pre-2.0 clips under the same 'Seedance 2' name, so the brand is not proof of the model. The exact asset examples/seedance2/4.mp4 first appears in Wayback on 2026-03-02.
Date unverifiable: the Commons date 2026-02-12 equals the official launch date, two days before the upload; it is not a generation date and no capture of the asset exists from before 2026-03-02.

Seedance 2.0 accepts up to 9 images, 3 video clips and 3 audio clips as references (official launch post), so a showcase clip can embed third-party inputs that a PD-algorithm tag cannot cover; provenance of inputs and prompt is unknown.
Content risk unknowable without viewing: title 'Husband coming home to his family' implies a family scene, possibly minors and lifelike people; 7 shots with real audio, 60 fps.

Hunter's claim that the showcase page has no Wayback snapshot is wrong (captures exist from 2026-02-14T19:39Z), but the snapshots reinforce, not weaken, the rejection: the showcase text says only 'Explore a curated collection of stunning AI-generated videos' with no reuse terms and no ByteDance attribution.
Metadata: ffprobe COMMENT tag 'vid:' (empty) is typical of ByteDance-pipeline transcodes but is not probative of Seedance 2.0 output.
No watermark/overlay detected by pixel statistics (0 % low-variance corner pixels), so the site logo may have been cropped out, which is itself a provenance red flag.

conditions: TREAT THE WHOLE VIDEO AS CC BY 4.0: it is an animation of two CC BY 4.0 photos by OWS Photography (both source pages verified: 'Creative Commons Attribution 4.0', AttributionRequired true), and the file's own structured data lists licence CC BY 4.0 (Q20007257) and status copyrighted (Q50423863).
